title: Efficient LLM Scheduling by Learning to Rank
technique: learning-to-rank predictor of relative output-length order to approximate SJF/SRTF in vLLM, with starvation prevention (max_waiting_time)

optimized_metrics.evidence: by scheduling requests on-the-fly based on the predicted rankings, we can approximate the SRTF/SJF schedule, hence reduce average latency and improve throughput, respectively
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: we can approximate the SRTF/SJF schedule, hence reduce average latency

optimized_metrics.evidence: by scheduling requests on-the-fly based on the predicted rankings, we can approximate the SRTF/SJF schedule, hence reduce average latency and improve throughput, respectively (batch generation)
Executing following SJF/SRTF may lead to starvation for long requests, whose users may wait very long to obtain a response.
our goal is to optimize the predictor model P to generate predictions with a larger Kendall's Tau, which are more correlated to the ground truth.

headline_claim.text: 2.8x lower latency in chatbot serving and 6.5x higher throughput in synthetic data generation

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For chatbot serving, we measure average and p90 per-token latency, which is the per-request latency divided by the output length.
metric_definitions.notes: s/token; per-request e2e latency / output length; mean and P90 across requests

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For offline synthetic generation tasks, we use throughput (requests/second) to indicate request generation speed.
Kendall's Tau coefficient [4] (we use the Kendall's Tau-b variant) can characterize the correlation between two rankings. Kendall's Tau ranges from -1 to 1.
metric_definitions.notes: proxy metric: similarity between predicted schedule and oracle SJF/SRTF; shown to correlate with lower latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we propose a max_waiting_time fairness metric to evaluate the fairness at per-request level
metric_definitions.notes: longest wait of any request; starvation measure

load_regime: request-rate sweep on real workloads (chatbot, ShareGPT/LMSYS-Chat-1M) plus offline burst of 2k requests for batch generation
tradeoff_acknowledged: SJF/SRTF may starve long requests; mitigated with starvation counter/priority quantum; predictor adds small overhead
hardware: DGX with 8x A100 40GB (NVLink); some experiments on single A100 80GB
workloads: ShareGPT, LMSYS-Chat-1M (1k requests per test for serving, 10k training samples)
extractor_notes: Latency in the headline is mean (and P90) per-token latency = e2e latency / output length (normalized). Intro states throughput and latency both desired; chatbot task targets latency, batch generation targets throughput. Kendall's Tau is an intermediate proxy objective for the predictor.
